sections.h2: Dale County and its housing market
sections.html:
Dale County occupies southeast Alabama's Wiregrass region, roughly forty miles from both Georgia and Florida. Its seat and biggest city is Ozark, and the county makes up the Ozark micropolitan area within the broader Dothan-Ozark region. Because the footprint is small, houses in Ozark, Daleville, Level Plains and the farm towns all answer to one county revenue office and one probate office.

Population was 49,326 in the 2020 census and is estimated at 49,912 for 2025. Of 22,761 housing units, 11.4 percent stand vacant. Homeowners occupy 59.6 percent of occupied units and renters 40.4 percent, which makes rentals a big slice of the market and puts many landlords among the sellers. Roughly 49.5 percent of residents live in urban areas.

Old deeds sometimes carry history. The county seat was once Dale's Court House, now Daleville, and later Newton before Ozark took over in 1870, so a parcel description that names one of those places may point to an older title chain. Title companies like a clean search before closing anywhere in the county.

Most of Fort Rucker lies inside Dale County, and the county commission describes it as the home of Army Aviation and a primary training base for military helicopter pilots. The county site now lists the post as Fort Novosel. Ozark and Daleville each border the installation, and military families come and go on orders.

A seller leaving on orders rarely has months to wait through showings and repairs. A direct cash sale with a short closing date fits that schedule and removes the worry of holding an empty house in another state. If that is you, ask the Revenue office for a payoff figure before you set the date, and give your title company a power of attorney if you will not be in town to sign.

The county has five cities and seven towns. The cities are Daleville, Dothan (partly in Houston and Henry counties), Enterprise (partly in Coffee County), Level Plains and Ozark. The towns are Ariton, Clayhatchee, Grimes, Midland City, Napier Field, Newton and Pinckard. Skipperville, Echo, Clopton, Kelly and Rocky Head are unincorporated. A home in an unincorporated place answers mainly to the county, while a city address adds city rules for code enforcement and utilities.

Schools vary by address. The Dale County School District serves most unincorporated areas. Daleville City Schools and Ozark City Schools cover their own cities, and Enterprise City Schools and Dothan City Schools cover the parts of those cities inside the county. Elementary students living on Fort Rucker attend Department of Defense Education Activity schools, and families on the post may choose Daleville, Enterprise or Ozark schools for the secondary grades. Buyers ask about zoning early, so work out which one applies to your house, and mention it in any listing or conversation. Zoning can matter more than a bedroom count to a family with children.

sections.h2: Due dates and the delinquency calendar
sections.html:
Dale County runs on the statewide calendar: the bill is due October 1 and any balance still open once December 31 passes is delinquent.

DateWhat happens
October 1Taxes due
January 1Taxes delinquent
FebruaryUnpaid accounts turned over to the Probate Court
MarchProbate Court meets
AprilProperties advertised for sale
MayTax sale

Assessment and collection sit with the county Revenue department, while deeds are recorded at the Probate Office. Get a payoff amount from Revenue first, then pick your closing date.

Taxes attach to the land and the house, never to a particular owner. Whoever holds title has to clear delinquent tax, including years from before they bought. For that reason the closing agent looks for open balances and subtracts them from what the seller receives.

Homestead status deserves a question at a sale. The regular homestead exemption is for a principal residence and can be claimed year round, so a buyer who moves in should ask the Revenue office how to file for it. If you are the seller, let the office know the house has changed hands.

At the closing table the title company prepares a statement that shows every deduction, with taxes, any mortgage payoff and recording costs listed before your net amount. Read it before you sign and ask about anything unfamiliar. If you are behind on more than one year, request a payoff for each year separately, since a single combined number can hide a year that was missed. Keep copies of the receipts, because they are your proof that the account was clear when you handed over the house.

Filing a deed triggers the privilege tax in Alabama Code section 40-22-1, which is fifty cents for every $500 of value. Probate staff collect it when the deed is filed, with a separate recording fee, and the proceeds divide two-thirds state, one-third county.

A deed must also come with proof of the true purchase price on the state revenue form. Hiding that proof knowingly, after the office requests it, can cost $100 or 25 percent of the tax, whichever is larger.

Think the value is too high? Talk to the Revenue office, then take it to the county Board of Equalization. Ask Revenue for the current protest dates before you file anything.

Section 40-3-25 lets you carry a board ruling to circuit court, but only within 30 days of the final decision. Keep paying: if the tax goes delinquent in the meantime, the appeal may be thrown out.

sections.h2: Common situations for Dale County sellers
sections.html:
Our calls tend to follow a handful of patterns, each on a different clock.

  • A vacant inherited house with years of tax unpaid.
  • A rental the owner can no longer afford to repair, with the tenant gone.
  • A military family that has left on orders while the house sits listed.
  • A house drifting toward the May tax sale after a January delinquency.

Our purchase covers back taxes at closing and takes the house in its current state. Timing matters most near the spring sale calendar. Three steps help in every case: obtain the payoff in writing, locate the deed, and name every owner who has to sign to the title company. An heir living out of state can sign in front of a notary at home, so distance need not hold up a closing. Ask the title company which forms it will accept.

Roads matter little here for the paperwork but plenty for buyers. U.S. 84 runs east and west, U.S. 231 runs north and south through the Ozark area, and state routes fill in the rest. There is no interstate, so commutes to Dothan and Enterprise use those routes, and a house near one of them is easier to show.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Dale County, Alabama?
faqs.a: October 1. They become delinquent after December 31, and unpaid accounts move to the Probate Court in February, with a tax sale in May.

faqs.q: Who assesses property in Dale County?
faqs.a: The Dale County Revenue office handles assessment and collection locally, and the Probate Office records deeds.

faqs.q: Do I owe back taxes if I inherit a Dale County house?
faqs.a: Yes. Alabama taxes follow the property, so unpaid years must be settled by the current owner. The balance is usually paid from sale proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: What is the deed tax on a Dale County sale?
faqs.a: Fifty cents per $500 of value under Alabama Code 40-22-1, plus the probate recording fee. Two-thirds goes to the state and one-third to the county.

faqs.q: Is Fort Rucker inside Dale County?
faqs.a: Most of it is. The post borders Ozark and Daleville, and the county site now lists it as Fort Novosel.
